subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu DM sessions rebuilt after gateway restart — duplicate keys + maintenance pruning

question: Should Feishu direct-message sessions be protected by a generic TTL-aware direct-DM retention rule, a Feishu-specific account/open_id validation and repair path, or both?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable fix changes session retention, account-scoped identity, and possible history repair behavior for existing Feishu users.

options.title: Combine TTL-aware DM retention with Feishu identity repair
options.body: Protect active/recent direct DM rows from maintenance while adding Feishu open_id validation plus a doctor or migration path for malformed/legacy direct keys.

options.title: Only document account-scoped workaround
options.body: Keep `per-account-channel-peer` as the official mitigation and defer pruning and malformed-key repair until live evidence narrows the remaining failure mode.

options.title: Blanket-protect all direct DM rows
options.body: Make all direct-message sessions durable by default, accepting potential unbounded store growth for high-volume one-off DM channels.

recommendation.title: Combine TTL-aware DM retention with Feishu identity repair
recommendation.body: Protect active/recent direct DM rows from maintenance while adding Feishu open_id validation plus a doctor or migration path for malformed/legacy direct keys.

likelyOwner.reason: They are already surfaced as the likely decision owner for the overlapping Feishu multi-bot identity boundary and can choose the durable account/session migration direction.
